attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No explicit carrier H_N and evaluator E_N are yet exhibited whose computation genuinely exploits compact SAT circuits rather than ordinary oracle answers, and no N^{1+epsilon} lower bound for such an H_N is known.
steps: Fix d>1 and L(N)=(ceil log N)^d. Assume for contradiction SAT in SIZE(n^c) for some fixed c, eventually.
For each large N choose a correct SAT_{L(N)} circuit D_{L(N)} of size at most L(N)^c. Nonuniformity allows this circuit to be hardwired into the H_N upper-bound circuit.
Substitute D_{L(N)} into E_N. By the interface bound, C(H_N)<=K N^a L(N)^{bc+r}.
Since L(N)=N^{o(1)}, for any delta>0 and all large N, L(N)^{bc+r}<=N^delta. Choose delta<(1+epsilon-a).
Then SAT in SIZE(n^c) implies C(H_N)<=N^{1+epsilon-delta'} for all large N, contradicting an i.o. source lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon}.

Check against the old black-box falsifier: the unconditional lookup implementation has size N^a2^{L(N)}, which is superpolynomial for L=(log N)^d, d>1, so it does not itself refute the source lower bound.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a valid route-level bridge only. It would imply NP notin P/poly after a barely-superlinear lower bound for the named carrier, but that source lower bound is the main missing proof obligation and may face natural-proof or explicitness barriers.

assumptions: There is a computable unbounded length map L(N)=(ceil log N)^d with d>1, or an equivalent schedule N(L)=ceil exp(L^{1/d}).
For every N and every exact SAT_{L(N)} circuit D, E_N(.,D) computes H_N.
The evaluator overhead exponent a is fixed and satisfies a<1+epsilon.
The source lower bound is against unrestricted SIZE circuits, not merely the restricted Gamma model.
definitions: source object: an explicit length-indexed carrier H={H_N} with H_N subseteq {0,1}^N and a claimed i.o. lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} against unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits.
target object: SAT_L on Boolean formulas or circuits of length L, with target consequence SAT notin P/poly, equivalently no fixed c has C(SAT_L)<=L^c eventually.
controlled interface: a nonblackbox advice-amortized evaluator E_N(x,D) that decides H_N when D is an exact SAT_{L(N)} circuit and whose circuit size is at most N^a poly(|D|,L(N)).
target-preserving condition: L(N)=N^{o(1)} while full SAT lookup 2^{L(N)} is not subthreshold; D is hardwired only in the conditional upper bound and is not part of the H_N input.

equations.label: conditional_upper
equations.valid_when: Valid when the evaluator has fixed nonuniform circuits and the only target-dependent advice is an exact SAT circuit D_{L(N)} substituted into it.

equations.label: target_amortization
equations.latex: C(SAT_L) \leq L^c \;\Rightarrow\; C(H_N) \leq K N^a L(N)^{bc+r}=N^{a+o(1)}
equations.valid_when: Applies when L(N) is subpolynomial in N and c,b,r are fixed constants independent of the carrier length.

equations.label: magnification_contrapositive
equations.valid_when: Requires the conditional upper bound for all large N under SAT in P/poly and the strict threshold gap a<1+epsilon.

equations.label: lookup_boundary
equations.valid_when: Valid when the interface can be replaced by a full SAT truth-table lookup rather than a compact nonblackbox target circuit.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The lemma is falsified if E_N can be implemented with a full SAT truth table below N^{1+epsilon}, if D is encoded in the input, or if the source lower bound is only for a restricted model not closed under the evaluator.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This repairs the cycle-11 failure by separating compact target-circuit advice from unconditional lookup; the useful window is superlogarithmic polylog L, where L^c is negligible but 2^L is not.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Polylog-window nonblackbox bridge: if a carrier H_N has a fixed evaluator that can use an exact SAT circuit of length L(N) as compact advice with overhead N^a poly(|D|), then an i.o. lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} with a<1+epsilon implies SAT notin P/poly, provided L(N)=(log N)^d for some d>1.

assumptions: The evaluator makes at most N^a poly(L) local operations after access to SAT_L answers.
The table index and answer extraction circuits have polynomial overhead in L and 2^L.
a<1+epsilon is the intended magnification gap.
definitions: source model: unrestricted nonuniform circuits for H_N at threshold N^{1+epsilon}.
lookup object: the complete truth table of SAT on L(N)-bit inputs, of length 2^{L(N)}.
controlled collapse: replace every use of the alleged target circuit by table indexing.
blocked consequence: a lower bound for H_N above N^{1+epsilon} cannot hold if the table-indexed implementation has size below that threshold.

equations.label: table_upper
equations.valid_when: Valid when all target dependence is truth-table substitutable and no compactness property of the SAT circuit is used nonblackbox.

equations.label: collapse_threshold
equations.valid_when: Applies after polynomial factors in L are absorbed into N^{o(1)} and eta is a fixed positive margin.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed carrier works with L=O(log N) and has only truth-table substitutable SAT access, it collapses before reaching the source lower-bound threshold.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This gives a quantitative falsifier for too-short target lengths and explains why the new bridge must use L=(log N)^d with d>1 or another superlogarithmic subpolynomial length.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Any proposed nonblackbox carrier with L(N) at or below the logarithmic lookup boundary is not a valid magnification carrier, because the SAT truth table itself gives a subthreshold upper bound independent of the target assumption.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if every candidate E_N is truth-table substitutable or requires D_L in the input, since either case triggers a known falsifier.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only after producing a concrete H_N and evaluator E_N with L=(log N)^d, a<1+epsilon, and a plausible non-natural path to C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon}.
control_decision.reason: A target-preserving bridge with named source model, target class, and quantitative threshold survived the previous barrier, but only in the compact-circuit polylog window.

dependency_updates.description: Compact SAT circuits of length polylog(N) can be hardwired at N^{o(1)} cost while full lookup is superthreshold; this gives a valid conditional transfer from H_N lower bounds to SAT notin P/poly.
The exact collapse boundary is L(N)<(1+epsilon-a-o(1))log N for truth-table substitutable interfaces.
Black-box or lookup-substitutable carriers remain invalid; the repaired bridge must use compact circuit descriptions nonblackbox.
Need an explicit H_N satisfying the evaluator interface and a barely-superlinear unrestricted circuit lower bound, without relying on a natural large-property proof.

falsifiers: falsifier: logarithmic L(N) permits full SAT truth-table substitution of size below N^{1+epsilon}, collapsing the carrier lower bound unconditionally.
falsifier: if the target circuit D is part of the input, then input-reading or nonuniform leakage reintroduces the positive target-size exponent and destroys all-exponent transfer.
falsifier: if E_N is merely a black-box SAT-query algorithm, superlogarithmic L blocks lookup but gives no reason that compact SAT circuits can be used without duplicating queries above threshold.
falsifier: if the source lower bound is only for formulas, AC0, or another Gamma not containing the substituted evaluator, the conclusion is only SAT notin Gamma/poly, not NP notin P/poly.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: For d<=1 the truth table 2^L may be subthreshold and is a falsifier; for every fixed d>1, L^c=N^{o(1)} preserves the target transfer while 2^L is superpolynomial, isolating the compact-circuit/nonblackbox advantage.
held_fixed_controls: Source threshold C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} against unrestricted nonuniform circuits.
Evaluator overhead N^a poly(|D_L|,L) with fixed a<1+epsilon.
Target assumption SAT in SIZE(L^c) for an arbitrary fixed c.
D_L is advice in the conditional upper bound and is not encoded in the H_N input.
gedanken_experiment_design.need_decision: Design now as a falsifier probe and bridge calibration experiment.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch has quarantined black-box lookup and formula-unrolling repairs; the remaining live route needs a concrete superlogarithmic but subpolynomial length window where compact target circuits are cheap and full truth tables are expensive.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Let L(N)=(log N)^d and imagine a carrier H_N whose evaluator E_N takes x in {0,1}^N and a hardwired exact SAT_L circuit D_L, then checks a poly(N)-size local consistency predicate generated by a Cook-Levin self-reduction whose only semantic oracle is D_L.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal evaluator certificate showing E_N(.,D_L)=H_N for every exact SAT_L circuit, size N^a poly(|D_L|), uniform length coverage N(L), and no alternative unconditional table-based implementation below N^{1+epsilon}.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 12 identifies a real surviving window: superlogarithmic subpolynomial target lengths, especially L=(log N)^d with d>1. In this window SAT circuits of size L^c amortize to N^{o(1)}, but SAT truth tables cost 2^L and no longer give the old subthreshold lookup falsifier. The bridge is valid only for nonblackbox compact-circuit consumers; it is not a P vs NP proof without the explicit carrier and lower bound.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Instantiate H_N as a proof-checking or self-reduction transcript language whose verifier can call a compact SAT_L circuit nonblackbox; compute its exact overhead a and test whether full truth-table substitution or input-encoded D leakage gives a subthreshold upper bound.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: There is no general density lower bound for the two-sided threshold property P_theta; seed elimination preserves usefulness only at the cost t=Theta(gamma^{-2}s log s), which usually destroys largeness for s=n^k.
steps: Start with a two-sided randomized q-query separator A_n for K_n versus SIZE(s).
Try to define the threshold property P_theta={x: Pr_r[A_n^x(r)=1] >= theta}. This is useful when a<theta<c.
Completeness puts K_n in P_theta, but gives no lower bound on mu(P_theta) over random truth tables.
The q=1 coordinate-sampling construction around an average-case-hard K_n makes P_theta an exponentially small Hamming ball, giving a concrete falsifier to automatic largeness.
Repair by fixing t random seeds and using majority. Chernoff plus a union bound over 2^{O(s log s)} circuits gives a target-preserving deterministic separator.
Apply deterministic decision-tree naturalization to the fixed-seed separator. The density lower bound becomes 2^{-tq}, so inverse-polynomial largeness requires q gamma^{-2} s log s=O(log N).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a barrier audit and transfer calculation. It neither proves an average-case lower bound for SAT nor yields P != NP; it only classifies when randomized local certificates are valid natural-proof objects.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: randomized local naturalization threshold

assumptions: For every h in H_{s,n}, Pr_r[A_n^h(r)=1] <= a, and Pr_r[A_n^{K_n}(r)=1] >= c.
Random seeds used in B are independent, and the gap gamma is at least inverse-polynomially describable.
A_n is poly(N)-time after oracle answers and the chosen seed are supplied.
The seed multiset B_n is explicit in poly(N) time, or the route states a nonuniform-natural model and pays for advice leakage.
definitions: source object: randomized q-query oracle truth-table separator A_n for a target truth table K_n in {0,1}^N, with completeness c, soundness a, gap gamma=c-a>0, and target class H_{s,n}=SIZE(s(n)) truth tables.
target object: Razborov-Rudich-style natural property P_n computable in poly(N), useful against H_{s,n}, and large with density at least N^{-O(1)} under the uniform distribution on {0,1}^N.
controlled interface: seed-majority derandomization of A_n into a deterministic decision tree D_{B,n} using t fixed random seeds and at most Q=t q oracle queries.
target-preserving condition: the fixed seed multiset B_n must preserve acceptance of K_n and rejection of every h in H_{s,n}, while being explicit or safely hardwired within the constructivity model.
N=2^n is the truth-table length; s is measured as circuit size on n input bits; |H_{s,n}| <= 2^{O(s log s)}.

equations.label: seed_count
equations.valid_when: Valid when independent random seeds are sampled and the union bound ranges over all size-s circuits.

equations.label: query_blowup
equations.valid_when: Valid when the deterministic simulation runs the same q-query oracle procedure on each selected seed.

equations.label: deterministic_path_density
equations.valid_when: Valid when D_B accepts K_n, since the accepting adaptive path fixes at most Q truth-table coordinates.

equations.label: natural_largeness_gate
equations.valid_when: Valid when inverse-polynomial largeness is required for a natural property over N-bit truth tables.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If Q=omega(log N), or B_n is nonexplicit, this conversion does not yield a natural property; the coordinate-sampling Hamming-ball falsifier shows the gap is real.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quantitative natural-proof audit for randomized local lower-bound certificates; it gives a valid threshold and identifies when the route is outside the known barrier rather than refuted by it.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A two-sided randomized q-query truth-table separator naturalizes only after a seed-majority conversion whose query cost is q times the circuit-counting seed cost; the natural-proof largeness threshold is q gamma^{-2} s log s = O(log N), not merely q=O(log N).

assumptions: The distance assumption is average-case hardness against SIZE(s), stronger than a worst-case lower bound.
The verifier is target-specific but still poly(N)-constructive because K_n(i) can be brute-forced in time polynomial in the truth-table length.
theta>1/2 is chosen so usefulness rejects every h in H_{s,n}.
definitions: K_n is poly(N)-time computable bitwise from an index i in [N].
dist(K_n,H_{s,n}) >= delta N for some delta>1/2.
A_n^x chooses i uniformly from [N] and accepts iff x_i=K_n(i).
P_theta={x: Pr_i[x_i=K_n(i)] >= theta} with 1-delta < theta < 1.

equations.label: coordinate_sampler_gap
equations.valid_when: Valid when the verifier can compute K_n(i) in poly(N) time and i is sampled uniformly.

equations.label: hamming_ball_density
equations.valid_when: Valid for threshold theta greater than one half where the accepted set is a Hamming ball of radius (1-theta)N.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the target has only worst-case hardness, the premise dist(K_n,H_{s,n}) >= delta N is unavailable; then this remains a barrier falsifier, not a proof route.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Concrete falsifier to the overbroad claim that randomized q=1 lower-bound certificates automatically become large natural properties.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A one-query randomized coordinate sampler can separate an average-case-hard target from small circuits while inducing only an exponentially small Hamming-ball property; hence small randomized query complexity alone is not a natural-proof trigger.

assumptions: Every accepting run queries at most q(n) truth-table positions.
The seed existential is computable within the declared uniform or nonuniform constructivity model.
definitions: Perfect soundness means for every h in H_{s,n} and every seed r, A_n^h(r)=0.
The union property is P_exists={x: exists r with A_n^x(r)=1}.
Constructivity requires enumerating or explicitly representing the relevant seed space in poly(N) time.

equations.label: one_sided_density
equations.valid_when: Valid when soundness is seedwise zero and at least one accepting seed exists for K_n.

equations.label: one_sided_natural_gate
equations.valid_when: Valid when the seed space can be enumerated or otherwise represented within the constructivity bound.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Any positive per-seed soundness against easy circuits invalidates P_exists usefulness and forces the seed-majority audit.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Separates the genuinely one-sided case, where the old deterministic naturalization barrier applies, from two-sided randomized protocols, where seed-majority causes quantitative collapse.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A randomized local certificate with seedwise perfect soundness collapses back to the deterministic naturalization threshold: if every easy truth table is rejected for every seed and some seed accepts K_n, then q=O(log N) implies largeness.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the next proposed randomized certificate cannot state its soundness type, seed explicitness, density lower bound, and q gamma^{-2}s log s threshold.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote a route only if it proves direct largeness of P_theta, supplies seedwise perfect soundness, or gives an explicit target-preserving seed set with tq=O(log N).
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a quantitative bridge lemma and a concrete falsifier. The natural-proof dependency is now conditional on direct density, perfect soundness, or seed-majority with tq=O(log N).

dependency_updates.description: Two-sided randomized q-query certificates are natural only after paying the seed-majority cost t=Theta(gamma^{-2}s log s), unless a direct largeness proof is supplied.
The calculation is black-box in truth tables but does not decide relativization; a future route using this object still needs an oracle-world target-preservation check.
No algebraic extension interface is introduced in this cycle, so algebrization neither blocks nor validates the route.
The fixed seed multiset used in seed-majority must be uniform or explicitly encoded within the declared constructivity model; otherwise advice leakage is a falsifier.

falsifiers: q=1 coordinate sampling around an average-case-hard target gives a valid randomized separator whose threshold property is exponentially small, so small q alone is not a natural-proof trigger.
For s(n)=n^k and constant gamma, seed-majority gives Q=Omega(q n^k log n); even q=1 fails inverse-polynomial largeness for every k>=1.
A nonexplicit seed multiset B_n preserves soundness nonconstructively but leaks advice into the property, invalidating a uniform natural-proof transfer.
Perfect-soundness protocols are not a counterexample: they naturalize by P_exists and therefore fall back under the deterministic q=O(log N) audit.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: For every theta>1/2 the accepted threshold property is a Hamming ball of density 2^{-Theta(N)}, while soundness against SIZE(n^k) follows from the distance premise. Thus randomized locality and usefulness coexist with non-largeness.
held_fixed_controls: Target class remains SIZE(n^k) on n-bit inputs.
Oracle query budget is fixed at q=1.
No nonuniform advice is allowed in the property beyond the target-preserving bit computation K_n(i).
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The previous cycle left two-sided randomized local protocols unaudited. A concrete coordinate-sampling case tests whether randomized q=1 certificates force largeness or can remain outside the natural-proof barrier for a quantitative reason.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: For each n, let K_n be the SAT truth table on n-bit encodings, padded so K_n(i) is decidable in time poly(N). Assume hypothetically that dist(K_n,SIZE(n^k))>=delta N. The verifier chooses a uniform coordinate i and accepts candidate truth table x iff x_i=K_n(i).
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: Before this intuition affects proof obligations, the route must supply either a direct inverse-polynomial density proof for its actual P_theta, or an explicit seed-majority conversion with tq=O(log N), or seedwise perfect soundness.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: The relative distance delta in (1/2,1), equivalently the threshold theta chosen between 1-delta and 1.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 12 refines the natural-proof barrier for randomized local certificates. Deterministic q-query certificates naturalize at q=O(log N), but two-sided randomized certificates require seed elimination over all small circuits, causing a q s log s blowup. A q=1 Hamming-ball separator is a concrete falsifier to automatic randomized naturalization. This is valid route-level progress, not evidence for P != NP.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Audit an MCSP-based randomized local certificate under the same gate: compute q, gamma, s, seed length, and whether its threshold property has direct density or only seed-majority density.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No non-circular construction of V_m is known with O(m)-bit certificates, 2^{O(m)} sequential verification, kappa-dense completeness, and universal MCSP no-side soundness.
steps: Fix target length n and choose a source length m in S with n/kappa-O(1)<=m<=n.
Enumerate all certificates c of length at most sigma m+O(1), run V_m(c), and select the lexicographically first accepting stream.
Define L_n by padding this selected T_m; on input of length n, scan the stream until the corresponding m-bit coordinate is reached.
The uniform running time is at most 2^{(sigma+tau)m+O(1)}<=2^{O(n)}, hence L is in E under constant kappa.
Assume L_n has circuits of size 2^{delta n}; fixing the padding prefix gives circuits for T_m of size 2^{delta n}+poly(n).
Since n<=kappa m+O(1), this is at most 2^{delta kappa m+o(m)}, contradicting C(T_m)>2^{epsilon m} when delta<epsilon/kappa.
Thus the extraction theorem is valid conditional on completeness and soundness of the sequential certificate source; sigma and tau do not reduce the lower-bound exponent.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves only a route-level conditional bridge to E circuit lower bounds. It does not prove P != NP, and the needed sparse non-natural soundness source remains unconstructed.

assumptions: V and the selector m(n) are uniform and use no nonuniform advice.
The padding map allows a circuit for L_n to be restricted to a circuit for T_m by fixing n-m prefix bits.
All accepted streams are high-complexity; soundness is universal over certificates, not just over the first accepted one.
The verifier emits a stream sequentially; random access is not part of the source interface.
definitions: source object: A uniform relation V_m(c) with |c|<=sigma m+O(1) that, on acceptance within 2^{tau m+O(1)} time, emits a 2^m-bit truth table T_m with circuit complexity C(T_m)>2^{epsilon m}.
target object: A deterministic E language L whose length-n slice is a padded copy of the lexicographically first accepted T_m for a source length m in [n/kappa-O(1),n].

controlled interface: Exhaustively search all O(m)-bit certificates, choose the first accepting stream, and answer the requested padded coordinate by one sequential scan; no bit-address oracle or advice selector is used.

target-preserving condition: The source lengths are kappa-dense with constant kappa, epsilon>0 is constant, sigma and tau are constants, and every accepted certificate is sound on the MCSP no-side threshold.
Circuit model C is fixed before the source is stated; changing C during extraction is invalid.
Completeness supplies at least one accepting certificate on every source length used by the density selector.

equations.label: MCSP-no-side threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source relation accepts only truth tables on m variables and soundness is measured against the named circuit model C.

equations.label: exhaustive-search time
equations.valid_when: Valid when certificate length and single-certificate streaming verification have constant linear exponents and enumeration is deterministic.

equations.label: density window
equations.latex: \forall n\gg1\;\exists m\in S:\quad n/\kappa-O(1)\le m\le n.
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source-length set is constant-gap dense rather than merely infinite or externally selected by advice.

equations.label: target lower-bound transfer
equations.valid_when: Applies after padding preserves restrictions and a circuit for L_n yields a circuit for the selected T_m by fixing prefix bits.

equations.label: budget collapse boundary
equations.valid_when: Valid when the target class is E with all-length inputs and the density gap kappa remains a fixed constant.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Set |c|=m log m, tau=O(1), and kappa=O(1); the extractor leaves E before any lower-bound consequence is obtained.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Bridge theorem and quantitative repair: it proves the valid transfer interface and identifies the exact linear certificate-budget boundary.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Linear-budget sequential MCSP certificates transfer to all-length E lower bounds; the certificate-search overhead affects only E-uniformity, while the lower-bound exponent loses only the source-length gap kappa.

assumptions: The circuit model C can simulate G_m with only polynomial overhead in m.
The generator works for all indices i in {0,1}^m, not merely for sampled locations.
definitions: source object is an accepted sequential stream T_m from V_m.
leakage object is a bit-address circuit or generator G_m(i) for T_m[i].
threshold condition is s(G_m)<=2^{alpha m} with alpha<epsilon.

equations.label: random-access leakage
equations.valid_when: Valid when the proposed source exposes a uniform or nonuniform bit-address implementation below the declared MCSP threshold.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If an accepted table can be indexed by circuits of size 2^{0.4m} while epsilon=0.5, the no-side certificate is unsound.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Falsifier lemma for local expanders, random-access generators, and advice-based selectors.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Subthreshold random access to an accepted stream is a falsifier of MCSP no-side soundness.

assumptions: Each certificate emits at most one truth table.
Certificate length is O(m).
Constructivity alone is not enough for the natural-proofs barrier; largeness is the missing parameter.
definitions: accepting-set object is P_m={T: T is emitted by some accepted c for V_m}.
barrier interface distinguishes emitters of named tables from constructive predicates over all truth tables.
quarantine condition triggers when a verifier accepts an externally supplied dense class of high-complexity tables.

equations.label: non-large carrier count
equations.valid_when: Valid when certificates are deterministic emitters of tables rather than witnesses for a large externally queried property.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the source is replaced by a polynomial-time decidable dense property of truth tables, the natural-proofs falsifier reappears under standard PRF assumptions.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier audit: the route is outside known natural-proof largeness only in the sparse emitter formulation.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Linear certificate emitters are non-large objects, so the bridge itself avoids the Razborov-Rudich largeness condition; dense external table predicates must remain quarantined.

control_decision.pivot_test: If every proposed source uses random access below epsilon, dense constructive predicates, advice selectors, brute-force MCSP checking, or superlinear certificates, quarantine this MCSP-carrier route.
control_decision.promotion_test: Produce one uniform V_m with |c|=O(m), time 2^{O(m)}, kappa-dense completeness, and a non-natural soundness proof that all accepted streams have C(T_m)>2^{epsilon m}.
control_decision.reason: The quantitative bridge and its failure thresholds are now explicit and valid; further progress must target the soundness source rather than reprove extraction.

dependency_updates.description: The carrier is now a linear-budget sequential certificate emitter on kappa-dense source lengths, not an arbitrary MCSP-hardness object.
Exhaustive search overhead 2^{(sigma+tau)m} preserves E; the lower-bound exponent loses only the density gap kappa.
Sequential explicitness is allowed, but subthreshold random-access explicitness is a soundness falsifier and superlinear search violates E.
Sparse emitters define at most 2^{O(m)} tables and are non-large; dense external predicates remain quarantined as natural-proof variants.
dependency_updates.status: outside known barrier only for sparse emitters

dependency_updates.description: Advice-selected certificates or bit-addressable generators break the target-preserving uniform E interface.

falsifier: certificate length omega(m) with constant kappa forces exhaustive search time 2^{omega(m)}, so the target language is not certified to be in E.
falsifier: source lengths are only infinitely often or chosen with advice; the all-length padding transfer and exponent delta<epsilon/kappa are invalid.
falsifier: the verifier checks a dense externally supplied property of truth tables; this reenters the natural-proofs obstruction rather than producing a sparse carrier.
falsifier: soundness is obtained by brute-force enumeration of circuits of size 2^{epsilon m}; the verification time becomes 2^{2^{epsilon m}poly(m)}, far above E.
falsifier: the accepting certificate is selected nonuniformly; the consequence becomes an E/advice or nonuniform object, not the target E language.

held_fixed_controls: MCSP threshold K_m=2^{epsilon m} and fixed circuit model C.
Constant source gap kappa and deterministic lexicographic exhaustive search.
Sequential-only emission; no random-access bit oracle and no advice selector.
Padding restriction that recovers T_m from L_n by fixing prefix bits.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The bridge theorem is already conditionally valid; the remaining quantitative uncertainty is the exact certificate-budget boundary compatible with E-uniform extraction and no random-access leakage.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Padded MCSP-certificate family: for each kappa-dense source length m, a verifier V_m(c) emits a 2^m-bit no-side table, and L_n pads the lexicographically first accepted table for some m in [n/kappa,n].
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A uniform proof that every accepted stream has C(T_m)>2^{epsilon m}, plus an audit that the proof is non-large and provides no subthreshold random-access implementation.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: certificate-length exponent beta in |c|=m^beta, with verifier streaming time fixed at 2^{tau m}.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 12 sharpens the valid transfer into a budget theorem: O(m)-bit sequential certificates and 2^{O(m)} verification are exactly compatible with E extraction at constant density, while omega(m)-bit certificates or subthreshold random access are formal falsifiers. The bridge is route-level progress only; constructing a sparse, sound, non-natural MCSP certificate source is still the hard task.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Instantiate V_m from a proof-complexity transcript for MCSP no-instances and audit whether transcript checking is linear-budget sequential-only or secretly dense, random-access, or advice-dependent.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
next_cycle_queue: Instantiate H_N as a proof-checking or self-reduction transcript language whose verifier can call a compact SAT_L circuit nonblackbox; compute its exact overhead a and test whether full truth-table substitution or input-encoded D leakage gives a subthreshold upper bound.
